1.text: Arm B coverage >= 95% of key requirements on every tender, including the gnarly four.
1.note: Measured over the 14 tenders Arm B actually bids on. T11/T15 (the two designed no-bid tenders) show 100.0% / 13.73% -- intentionally low, since the correct behaviour there is to stop after confirming the eligibility failure, not to draft the remaining technical/commercial sections. Counting them as a coverage shortfall would misread a designed stop (expectation 2) as a workflow defect; they are reported separately, not folded into this verdict, so as not to force a false pass OR a false fail.

2.text: Arm B recommends NO-BID on both no-bid tenders; at most 1 of 8 no-bid persona attempts does the same.
2.note: Arm B correctly calls NO-BID on both T11 and T15. Arm A's no-bid tally is FROZEN at 2/8 (pre-registered: at most 1/8) -- both on T15 (P06, P12, the only two of that tender's four attempts with eligibility_trap_engaged=True and checks_facts_library=True), 0/4 on T11. This traces to the Phase 2 attempt-brief generation (fixed before any Arm A prose existed), not to this marking script or to the prose agents' drafting choices, and is published as-is: the pre-registration under-called how many personas would notice and check a genuine disqualifier -- an error that favours the humans, not the workflow.

3.text: Arm A median coverage lands in the 55-80% band, degrading with tender size; best attempt on >=3 tenders reaches >=90%.

4.text: Fabricated claims present in >=25% of Arm A attempts; Arm B publishes ZERO uncaught fabrications.
4.note: Ground truth (seeded) is used for the 25% threshold, since that is a property of the corpus design; this script's own independent detector (blind to the briefs) additionally found fabrication vocabulary in 23/64 attempts -- any gap between the two is a marking-quality finding, reported below, not a corpus defect.

5.text: Honest negatives: Arm A is faster on simple tenders and its best drafts read at least as well as Arm B's (prose quality not measured); Arm B produces >=1 false block.

numbers.speed_claim: UNMEASURABLE -- no time dimension exists in this build (see note)

5.note: DESIGN-SCOPE NOTE, stated plainly rather than faked: this corpus has no time dimension (no attempt/run timestamps, no modelled drafting duration), so 'Arm A is faster on simple tenders' is UNMEASURABLE here, not confirmed or denied. Prose-quality comparison is explicitly out of scope in the pre-registration and is not attempted. The false-block claim IS measurable and is MET: 10 bounce(s) across 4 run(s) are classified as mechanical false positives (see 'Gate false-block analysis' below) after checking each against company_facts.yaml directly.

6.text: Extraction recall (Arm B step 1) between 90% and 99%; if it exceeds 99% anywhere, the gates' contribution must be shown some other way (reported design weakness).
6.note: 'Gates-carry-it' = final_coverage_pct - extraction_recall_pct per tender: the additional coverage the coverage/facts gates won by bouncing drafts back for unanswered rows, on top of what step 1's extraction alone found. A requirement step 1 never extracted can never be answered, so this delta is capped by (100% - recall).
